FIRMWARE / 02

title: Make sense of the field.
text:
One control tick
The board driver establishes a nominal 16 MHz HSI clock, 1 MHz SPI1, 125000-baud USART1, a 1 MHz TIM2 timestamp, and a 1 ms SysTick. The main scheduler exchanges a 16-byte packet with the FPGA, checks its validity and freshness, and then updates control state.
Exchange and validate.Send the previous current request; receive the next telemetry snapshot. Check checksum, faults, and sample progression.Estimate the state.Convert current and Hall readings using measured scaling and calibration. Estimate and filter downward velocity.Compute the request.Ramp the gap target and apply position feedback, saturation, and anti-windup.Service the interface.Poll UART without waiting for characters. Continue page transmission across control ticks.

title: Make sense of the field.
text:
Control law
error = measured_gap − ramped_target
current_request = clamp(
    hover_current + Kp·error + Kd·filtered_velocity + integral,
    0, maximum_current
)
Derivative acts on measurement to avoid a setpoint kick. The integrator updates only when the request is unsaturated or the error drives it out of saturation. Current-test mode uses a separate current ramp and requires the object to be supported.
Default gains and bias are zero. Scaling, calibration coefficients, operating bounds, and gains are configuration inputs awaiting measurements. They are not working levitation settings.

title: Make sense of the field.
text:
The operator interface
The existing course ESP8266 firmware is used unchanged. The MCU serves a compact interface with height and current-test modes, arm/clear/stop controls, and raw plus engineering-unit telemetry. A five-second browser lease stops an abandoned session.
This portfolio documents that interface; it does not connect to or energize a physical coil.

title: Make sense of the field.
section: Deadlines are part of the design
text:
Deadlines are part of the design
A missed update, invalid telemetry, stalled sample ID, or reported fault stops the coil. The design budgets roughly 2–3 ms worst-case outer measurement-to-actuation delay, including scanning, scheduling, packet transfer, and PWM boundaries. That estimate must be checked on the bench.
At 1 MHz, a 128-clock exchange plus chip-select guards takes at least 132 µs, before software gaps. Page formatting and transmission must fit alongside control work; overruns are faults rather than silently skipped updates.

Coil and object come first
A holding-force rating at contact does not establish useful levitation force across an air gap. Start with an instructor-approved test coil and measure force versus current and gap, winding resistance, inductance, and steady temperature.

title: Proposal working draft: Hall-sensed magnetic levitator
text:
Skip to content







Documentation / Technical guide

Proposal working draft: Hall-sensed magnetic levitator
Readiness: an implementation proposal for team review, not an already validated promise. First confirm the feasible object and gap interval; then replace candidate numerical specifications with the team’s committed values and paginate the prose to the course limit. Supporting diagrams, calculations, schedule, and BOM are linked below.
We will build a single-axis magnetic suspension using the E155 STM32L432KC and UPduino v3.1. An overhead electromagnet will support an object containing a permanent magnet. Two linear Hall sensors and a measured coil-current signal will estimate its vertical gap. A local Wi-Fi webpage will select a bounded gap target, show estimated gap/current/fault status, and stop operation. A capped current-test mode will support calibration and debugging while the object is mechanically supported.
The proposed acceptance specification is continuous suspension for 30 seconds, operation at three commanded gaps in a validated interval initially targeted at 8–14 mm, steady mean gap error no greater than 0.5 mm after settling, and recovery from a small recorded disturbance. A current cap, loss-of-command timeout, and physical interlock will remove drive when required. A separate reference measurement will evaluate actual height; the Hall estimate alone will not establish accuracy. Feasibility testing may require a narrower interval before this proposal is committed.
The MCU will perform calibrated field compensation, filtered velocity estimation, 1 kHz PD/PID position control, target ramping, UART communication with the course ESP8266, and 1 MHz SPI exchanges with the FPGA. The FPGA will acquire current and both Hall channels through an MCP3204, run a fixed-point 10 kHz PI current controller, generate 20 kHz PWM, validate commands, and apply autonomous fault/watchdog supervision. These functions continue while the MCU formats and transmits pages.
The largest technical risk is separating object position from coil field across changing current, temperature, and object orientation. We will test this first using known gaps and currents, then validate a local estimator on an independent sweep. If the estimator cannot meet the proposed error bound, the geometry/object/sensor arrangement must change before claiming a working height loop. A steel-only sphere requires explicit current-dependent characterization and is not assumed compatible with the initial estimator.
The power circuit uses a separately supplied coil, low-side MOSFET and gate driver, an inline current shunt/amplifier inside the flyback loop, and a physical E-stop/current comparator interlock. Coil force across an air gap, current response, and continuous heating will determine final component ratings. Default firmware and HDL are disabled until bring-up gates pass.
See system diagram, control equations, and performance calculations, candidate BOM, and six-week division of work. All non-course parts remain unpurchased; budget entries are allowances awaiting exact quotes and stockroom confirmation. Team names, confirmed budget, and the feasible operating interval must be settled before submission.

title: Candidate hardware and proposed wiring
text:
Parts and early decision

Two TI DRV5055 linear analog Hall sensors, initially evaluate A3 or A4 sensitivity. Choose the full ordering code/package after measuring field range. These are analog sensors, not magnetic switches. Power them at 3.3 V with local 100 nF bypassing; use the same quiet rail for the ADC reference. The manufacturer datasheet specifies the transfer range, orientation, and bandwidth. Verify package pin numbering; TO-92 and SOT-23 differ.
One MCP3204-CI/P 12-bit ADC at 3.3 V, with CH0 current, CH1 primary Hall, CH2 reference Hall, and unused CH3 tied to analog ground. See the MCP3204 datasheet. The FPGA drives this bus independently of the MCU bus.
One INA240A1 amplifier, gain 20, and a 0.100 ohm precision shunt in series with the coil. At 3.3 V, ground both REF inputs for unidirectional measurement. Account for zero-current output headroom/offset in calibration. Its datasheet describes common-mode behavior and PWM rejection. An SOIC adapter or assembled board is needed if using a bare IC.
A MOSFET with verified on-resistance at the actual gate voltage, a gate driver such as UCC27511, and a flyback diode rated above coil current and supply/transient voltage. Driver inputs, supply bypassing, and gate discharge follow its datasheet. A 5 V driver supply is a candidate, subject to the selected MOSFET.
A separate current-limited coil supply, fuse, physical E-stop, current comparator, output logic, and a nonmagnetic frame with a catch tray. Coil voltage/current, fuse, diode/clamp, MOSFET, threshold circuit, and thermal ratings remain contingent on the coil.

Start with an instructor-approved stockroom coil or one inexpensive test coil. Determine the usable gap with a force measurement and temperature test. A manufacturer’s holding force at contact does not establish levitation capacity. Check whether a permanent-magnet object rotates, sticks to the core, or produces ambiguous Hall readings. A steel-only object requires a different field identification experiment before this estimator can be adopted.
The candidate BOM contains budget allowances, not live supplier quotes. Replace all allowance values with dated quotes, full ordering numbers, stockroom availability, shipping, and tax before submitting or purchasing. The course currently marks the purchasing policy as under construction; confirm it with the instructors.

title: Candidate hardware and proposed wiring
text:
Power circuit connectivity
The netlist defines the circuit nodes. This is a design sketch; it must become a labeled KiCad schematic using the selected packages and ratings before the final report.
flowchart LR
    PS[Coil supply positive] --> F[Fuse / E-stop power contact]
    F --> V[Node VCOIL]
    V --> R[Inline shunt 0.100 ohm]
    R --> L[Coil]
    L --> D[MOSFET drain]
    D --> Q[MOSFET source to power ground]
    D -->|flyback: anode → cathode| V
    R -. Kelvin sense .-> A[Current amplifier]
    A --> ADC[ADC CH0]
    A --> C[Overcurrent comparator]
    C --> E[Healthy interlock]
The flyback diode cathode connects to VCOIL before the shunt. That places both coil and shunt inside the recirculation loop, so off-time current is measured. A shunt placed only in the supply lead outside that loop does not measure recirculating current. The diode protects the MOSFET but yields slow decay; measure whether this is adequate. Replacing it with a higher-voltage clamp requires rechecking MOSFET/common-mode/supply stress and retuning.
Hardware must force the driver inactive whenever PWM is low, FPGA enable is low, MCU permit is low, or the physical interlock is unhealthy. For example, use 3.3 V AND logic to combine these conditions into the driver’s noninverting input; tie its inverting input low. Keep a gate-source pulldown and logic-input pulldowns so an unconfigured FPGA cannot energize the coil. The physical E-stop also opens coil power. Derive fault_n from the E-stop auxiliary contact and an overcurrent comparator with a defined safe default; its exact schematic/threshold depends on the chosen current limit. Never tie fault_n permanently high in the powered levitator.
For the numerical example, 0.5 A produces about 1.0 V at the current amplifier, or 1241 ADC counts. A separate comparator threshold must be established from actual offsets, gain tolerance, and thermal/current ratings. FPGA sampling is not a substitute for this physical cutoff. Software shutdown removes drive; stored magnetic energy still decays through the flyback path.

title: Build, simulate, and program
text:
MCU: GNU Arm toolchain
Install CMake, Ninja or Make, and GNU Arm Embedded GCC. Supply the device headers containing stm32l432xx.h/system_stm32l4xx.h and the CMSIS core headers containing core_cm4.h. Your course repository already contains both under lab/lab07/lab07_mcu/lab07_proj. Do not copy generated lab outputs into this repository.
From the repository root in PowerShell:
$course = '..\hmc-e155\lab\lab07\lab07_mcu\lab07_proj'
cmake -S firmware -B build/mcu -G Ninja `
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=arm-gcc.cmake `
  -DSTM32_DEVICE_INCLUDE="$((Resolve-Path "$course/STM32L4xx/Device/Include").Path)" `
  -DCMSIS_CORE_INCLUDE="$((Resolve-Path "$course/CMSIS_5/CMSIS/Core/Include").Path)"
cmake --build build/mcu
Outputs: build/mcu/maglev.elf, maglev.hex, and maglev.map. GNU extensions are used for the vector table. The linker reserves the main 48 KiB SRAM bank and at least 4 KiB stack; the separate 16 KiB SRAM2 is unused. Standard C library support is supplied by GNU Arm with nosys stubs; floating-point printf is unnecessary.
Program the HEX through ST-LINK using STM32CubeProgrammer or your lab’s established programming workflow. Select STM32L432KC, connect/reset, load the built image, verify, then run with coil power disconnected. The ST-LINK serial port is not the ESP8266 link used here.

title: The architecture of balance.
text:
Define the direction first
The gap xx is measured downward from the coil reference plane. Increasing the target lowers the object. A simplified local force balance is
mẍ=mg−F(i,x).m\ddot{x}=mg-F(i,x).
The rough relation F≈ki2/x2F\approx ki^2/x^2 helps identify the system, but it is not a validated model of the eventual coil. Mass, lift, resistance, inductance, and temperature must be measured for the chosen geometry.

title: The architecture of balance.
text:
Two loops, different responsibilities
The position loop uses the measured gap error and filtered downward velocity to request current. A positive error means the object is too low, so the controller requests more lift. A rate-limited target, saturation, and anti-windup bound that request.
The inner loop regulates measured current in ADC counts. Its fixed-point PI calculation updates the next PWM duty. Normal updates occur at period boundaries; a fault can remove the output immediately.
STM32L432KCMCU design ↗Follow the estimate, control law, scheduler, and interface.LATTICE iCE40UP5KFPGA design ↗Inspect acquisition, arithmetic, PWM, and fault supervision.

title: The architecture of balance.
text:
The central experiment: observability
Both Hall sensors see the coil and the suspended object. Two readings do not automatically cancel the coil field. The local estimator also uses measured current:
gap_mm = c0 + c1·Hall1_counts + c2·Hall2_counts + c3·current_A
Calibration requires known mechanical gaps, current sweeps, and independent holdout measurements. Because channels are sampled sequentially, changing current during a scan may corrupt compensation. Fixed-object current steps are a necessary test before feedback tuning.
The first object should contain a permanent magnet with repeatable orientation. A plain steel sphere is not interchangeable with that design assumption.

title: The architecture of balance.
text:

Establish the physical system.Select a coil and object; measure force, field range, and heating.Validate sensing and shutdown.Check analog scaling, Hall observability, interlock behavior, and timing.Close the current loop.Use supported-object current steps and measured response to tune the PI controller.Close the position loop.Tune PD first, then evaluate settling, disturbance rejection, and operating limits.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
Skip to content
Documentation / Technical guide

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 1. Establish sensing feasibility before a parts commitment
text:
1. Establish sensing feasibility before a parts commitment
Mount the candidate coil and actual object at known gaps using nonmagnetic spacers. Measure both Hall voltages with no object, with the object, and at multiple coil currents. Choose sensor orientation/sensitivity so signals remain in their linear range and neither clips. Measure whether object position remains distinguishable after coil-current effects and noise are included. Sweep the gap in both directions to expose hysteresis, rotation, and ambiguous responses. For a plain steel sphere, explicitly check the current-dependent magnetization model rather than adopting the permanent-magnet assumptions.
Acceptance: at least one contiguous operating interval has repeatable position estimates with independent holdout RMSE ≤0.25 mm and worst error ≤0.5 mm. These are proposed design thresholds; revise the committed specification with the team/instructor before proposal submission if feasibility measurements require it. Stop expanding the system if observability fails; change geometry/sensor arrangement/object first.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
2. Characterize coil and driver
Measure coil DC resistance cold and hot, inductance or current step response, lift force versus current and gap, current needed to support the measured object mass, and temperature rise. Select supply, switch, clamp, wiring, fuse, current cap, and mechanical clearance from those measurements. Establish a continuous-duty current rating or add a thermal cutoff in the physical interlock. The supplied code does not measure coil temperature.
Acceptance: lift exceeds weight with operating margin throughout the chosen interval; thermal and electrical ratings support the intended demo duration. Document tau=L/R, maximum current rise/decay rates, Pcoil=I²R, switch/shunt dissipation, and clamp voltage. Do not power the coil through the development board or a solderless breadboard power rail.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 3. Verify digital paths with coil power disconnected
text:
3. Verify digital paths with coil power disconnected
Check bridge switches open and every jumper by continuity. Program default-disabled devices. Confirm the UART baud and complete HTML. Capture host SPI and ADC SPI: mode 0, clock rates, CS guards, 128-bit host frames, CRC byte ordering, 24 ADC clocks, channel order, and CS high interval. Apply known analog voltages to the ADC channels. Compare raw telemetry against a meter. A plausible constant ADC code is not sufficient proof that an ADC is connected.
Acceptance: decoded measurements match applied voltages and the C/SV packet tests. Scope sample_debug and PWM to verify rate and acquisition phase; output remains low during reset, programming, power loss, and disconnected permit/interlock.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 4. Calibrate and prove the physical cutoff
text:
4. Calibrate and prove the physical cutoff
Support the object; initially replace the coil with a resistive load if suitable for the driver. Calibrate current zero and gain against a meter, including low-current output headroom. Compute the firmware absolute code limit and FPGA compiled ceiling from actual calibration; account for tolerances. Check the inline shunt measures flyback current. Set and measure the comparator threshold/hysteresis independently. Operate the E-stop and break each interlock wire while monitoring the actual MOSFET gate.
Acceptance: no unintended pulse at startup; physical fault removes gate drive promptly even if the MCU and FPGA are halted. Record the measured gate-off delay and coil-current decay separately. Only then set power_stage_ready=true and LEV_COMMISSIONED=1 with low supply/current limits, still supported mechanically. Keep calibration_ready=false.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
5. Tune the inner current loop
Select current-test mode while stopped. Start at zero target. Begin with Ki zero and small Kp; increase until current follows small supported-load steps without sustained ringing. Add a modest Ki to remove steady error. Convert gains into the documented Q8.8 per-sample units. Examine response across PWM duty and supply voltage. Avoid integral gains below one representable step unless a different fixed-point scale is implemented.
Acceptance: no sustained oscillation, no saturation under nominal commands, bounded overshoot, and measured response sufficiently faster than the intended position loop. Sweep current through the allowed range and verify the cap. Test MCU cable removal, identical frozen packets, checksum errors, missed updates, ADC disconnect, comparator trip, permit loss, and E-stop. An ADC disconnect can yield a plausible stuck value; the physical cutoff remains necessary. Retain scope captures, not just a pass checkbox.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
section: 6. Fit Hall calibration and tune the position loop
text:
6. Fit Hall calibration and tune the position loop
Follow docs/calibration.md with current control already characterized. Fit only a validated local operating region. Verify sensor sign by moving the supported object downward at fixed current: reported gap must increase. Measure false position change after a current step with the object clamped. Set measured operating range, coefficients, hover current, and candidate PD gains in config.c. Validate by recompiling and running host checks before setting calibration_ready=true.
At the nominal gap, use a catch tray, a current-limited supply, and a supported release. Tune PD for damping before adding integral. Expand the commanded range gradually. Record recovery from small disturbances and current saturation. Test the full path while refreshing web pages repeatedly to check the MCU deadline budget.

title: Staged bring-up and acceptance gates
text:
7. Demonstrate and preserve evidence
Proposed final demonstration: stable suspension for 30 seconds; three gap targets in the measured usable interval; mean error ≤0.5 mm at each after settling; recovery from a small documented disturbance; page-based stop and current cap; and physical interlock operation. Record target/estimated gap versus an independent ruler/camera reference, current, PWM, peak error, settling time, RMS noise, and coil temperature. Do not call the Hall estimate independent ground truth.
Complete the checkoff matrix, final KiCad schematics, photos, team information, and demo video. Upload/publish only when the team has reviewed the actual evidence and the instructor’s current submission requirements.

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Skip to content
Documentation / Technical guide

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Measurements
Use a fixed jig and known gap reference. Log gap_mm,hall1,hall2,current_a rows in CSV; data/calibration-format.csv gives the header. Measure actual current, not just commanded current. Sample a grid of gaps and currents spanning the proposed operating interval, with repeated measurements after reversing each sweep. Include coil-only baseline, object orientation, supply, temperature, sensor mount dimensions, and ADC filter components in the experiment notes.
Use a second independently collected sweep for holdout validation. Randomly splitting adjacent samples from one stationary measurement understates error. Repeat across relevant coil temperatures and several current trajectories. Hold the object fixed during current steps to quantify how much coil-field change leaks into estimated position. A static fit may pass while sequential-channel transient error makes feedback unusable.
The local affine model is a practical first model, not a physical cancellation guarantee. Nonmonotonic or degenerate sensor responses require a change of placement, object, sensitivity, or estimator. A table/nonlinear estimator is a future design change if the local fit fails; it is not silently implemented by the calibration script. Restrict the committed gap/current interval to where this model has been validated.

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Fit and validate
python -m pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python tools/calibrate.py data/raw/training.csv data/raw/holdout.csv
The script normalizes inputs, checks matrix rank and conditioning, fits least squares, prints training/holdout errors, and emits candidate hall_c coefficients only when numerical acceptance passes. It rejects near-rail Hall samples and a holdout current/gap range outside the training range. It does not change firmware or enable outputs. Save reviewed coefficients and measured validity ranges in config.c; preserve data deliberately under data/results when suitable for the public repository. Files under data/raw are ignored by default.
Current conversion is I=(ADC-current_zero)/counts_per_amp. Fit zero/gain against an independent meter over the intended range. Convert an absolute trip current into round(current_zero + counts_per_amp * Itrip) and choose a conservative threshold accounting for uncertainty. Keep the FPGA ceiling, command limit, comparator, and firmware cap consistent. The runtime cap should remain below the physical trip threshold.

title: Hall/current calibration and controller tuning
text:
Gains and practical limits
The height loop uses mm, A, and seconds: Kp has A/mm; Kd has A·s/mm; Ki has A/(mm·s). Begin with Ki zero. Verify lift direction on a supported object before release. The current loop uses ADC counts and PWM ticks, with Ki already multiplied by 0.0001 s. Quantizing a small Ki to zero changes loop behavior; verify the quantized loop rather than only the floating-point design.
Tune around one measured equilibrium. The force model may change significantly with gap. hover_a is a constant bias in this implementation; there is no unvalidated gain scheduling or feedforward lookup. The feasible height interval may therefore be smaller than the candidate 8–14 mm values. Browser targets and fault limits must be updated to match the tested interval. Sampling rate, delay, sensor filtering, coil decay, object mass, and lateral/orientation motion all affect stability.

title: Implementation and control design
text:
System boundary
One coil controls vertical motion. The initial object should contain a permanent magnet with a repeatable orientation, so its field can be distinguished from the coil field. A plain steel sphere is not a drop-in equivalent: its induced field varies with current and gap. Do not assume the supplied affine estimator can sense it. Validate the actual object and geometry before committing the proposal.

This is a useful hardware/software partition, not a claim that an STM32 cannot generate 20 kHz PWM. The FPGA’s substantial work is autonomous ADC sequencing, fixed-point feedback, packet validation, independent watchdogs, and output gating. The MCU contributes sensor compensation, filtered velocity estimation, floating-point position control, trajectories, and communication.

title: Implementation and control design
text:
Coordinates and model
Let x be the gap in mm measured downward from the coil reference plane. Increasing the web target lowers the object. Locally,
m*x_ddot = m*g - F(i,x), with a rough magnetic model F ≈ k*i²/x².
The force law is an identification aid, not a validated model of a stock electromagnet. Equilibrium requires measured force at the actual air gap, not a zero-gap holding-force rating. Record mass, lift versus current/gap, resistance, inductance, and steady temperature. Current dynamics approximately satisfy L*di/dt = Vdrive - R*i; off-time decay depends on the clamp.
Hall outputs contain the object field, the coil field, offsets, and noise. The supplied local estimator is
gap_mm = c0 + c1*H1_counts + c2*H2_counts + c3*measured_current_A.
Coefficients come from a mechanically fixed object swept through known gaps and currents. Two Hall sensors do not automatically cancel the coil. The ADC is multiplexed, so changing current during the scan can also corrupt this compensation. Validate transient errors; narrow the operating range or change sensing/model if necessary.
The MCU uses e = measured_gap - ramped_target and
Irequest = clamp(Ihover + Kp*e + Kd*filtered_velocity + integral, 0, Imax).
Positive error and positive downward velocity request more lift. Derivative acts on measurement to avoid setpoint kick. Target gap moves at a bounded rate. Integral updates only when the output is unsaturated or the error drives it out of saturation. Default gains and bias are zero; tune PD first. Height-mode arming initializes the ramp at the requested gap, so initially hold the object close to that target. Current-test mode ramps current separately and requires a supported object.

title: Implementation and control design
text:
FPGA pipeline





%%{init: {"theme":"base","themeVariables":{"primaryColor":"#edf0e8","primaryTextColor":"#202824","primaryBorderColor":"#95a08d","lineColor":"#77846f","fontFamily":"Segoe UI","fontSize":"16px"}}}%%
flowchart TB
    T[24 MHz timebase] --> P[1200-cycle PWM phase]
    T --> Q[2400-cycle ADC frame]
    Q --> A[CH0 current → CH1 Hall → CH2 Hall]
    A --> R[Coherent scan snapshot + sample ID]
    A --> I[Signed Q8.8 current PI]
    I --> L[Clamp 0…1080 ticks]
    L --> P
    S[SPI frame + CRC + sequence check] --> I
    S --> W[20 ms command watchdog]
    A --> V[250 us scan watchdog + current limit]
    W --> G[Latched fault/output gate]
    V --> G
    P --> G






Current PI takes error in raw ADC counts. kp_q8/256 is duty ticks per count. ki_q8/256 is duty ticks per count per 100 us update, already including the sample interval. Signed intermediate widths are bounded explicitly (13-bit error, 27-bit proportional product, 24-bit integral increment, 28-bit sums, and 21-bit integrator); accepted gain bounds are 4096 and 1024, and the integrator is bounded to ±1080×256. PWM duty changes only at a period boundary. A fault or loss of permit can truncate a pulse immediately. Zero enable clears PI history. Seven registered arithmetic stages finish in less than 0.3 us. CRC engines process one payload bit per clock; command validation completes about 5 us after CS rises. Status is assembled once per 100 us frame and its checksum is completed before the next scan. Fault decisions have a few system clocks of register latency beyond the nominal intervals; physical output gating is independent of telemetry refresh.
Fault bits are 0 external interlock, 1 sampled overcurrent, 2 command timeout, and 3 ADC scan timeout. Faults latch. Clearing requires a disabled valid command, recent completed scan, healthy external input, and current below the requested hard limit. Clear and arm are separate actions. A bad checksum, malformed frame, or repeated sequence cannot refresh the command watchdog.

title: Implementation and control design
text:
MCU routine responsibilities
board_init establishes a 16 MHz HSI clock, 1 MHz SPI1, 125000-baud USART1, 1 MHz TIM2 timestamp, and 1 ms SysTick. Main checks elapsed ticks, exchanges one packet, detects stalled sample IDs, estimates gap/current, and computes the next output. Missing a tick or seeing invalid/stale telemetry stops the coil. UART RX/TX are polled without waiting for characters; page transmission continues across control updates. Requests are bounded and matched exactly. A 5-second browser lease stops an abandoned session. Measure worst-case execution time including page formatting; an overrun is a fault, not skipped control work.

title: Communication contract v1
text:
MCU ↔︎ FPGA SPI
Separate bus from the ADC. Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), MSB first, 1 MHz maximum. CS leads the first rising SCK and follows the last falling SCK by at least 2 us. Clock exactly 128 bits under one CS. No bytes are read from MCU struct memory directly: the C codec packs explicit big-endian fields.
CRC is CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: polynomial 0x1021, initial 0xffff, no reflection, no final XOR, over bytes 0–13; stored high byte first at 14–15. Check vector 123456789 → 0x29b1.

Telemetry is the most recently prepared coherent scan/status snapshot, frozen at CS assertion; it is not the response to the command currently being transmitted. Status is rebuilt every 100 us. The command is accepted about 5 us after CS rises once its frame/CRC/bounds are valid. There is no command ACK field; confirm actual enable/fault state in subsequent telemetry. A rejected command cannot keep the output enabled indefinitely: the 20 ms watchdog still runs. MCU command IDs change every tick, including disabled packets; the FPGA rejects the immediately repeated ID. This detects frozen retransmission, not arbitrary network replay/security attacks.
The accepted hard limit must be positive and no greater than the compiled FPGA ceiling. Targets use the ADC’s absolute code, including measured current zero offset. The hard limit also uses absolute counts; update both firmware and FPGA configuration together. Gain formats and fault bits are defined in docs/design.md. The MCU faults on invalid telemetry or on a sample ID unchanged for 3 ms. Flags indicate a completed scan, not electrical proof that an ADC is connected: a stuck but plausible MISO level cannot be fully diagnosed digitally.

title: Communication contract v1
text:
ESP8266 ↔︎ MCU
Use the course IoT server at 125000 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit. Its line format is /REQ:<route>\n. This implementation accepts CRLF too. Routes are short, exact strings: empty route reads the page; arm, stop, clear, modegap, modeamp, up, and down perform controls. Query parameters are unnecessary. Connect to the board’s existing SSID, then open http://192.168.4.1/.
Each response is one HTML document from <!DOCTYPE html> through </html>. The course bridge forwards HTML rather than a general JSON API. The page refreshes the root once per second so a refresh does not repeat an arm or increment command. Every recognized request renews the 5-second browser lease. A backgrounded browser or lost Wi-Fi therefore stops the system. The UART page path never blocks while waiting for bytes. Web STOP depends on communications and is distinct from the physical interlock.

Limits of these checks
No boards or instruments were attached. No real lift, height accuracy, thermal behavior, analog bandwidth, wiring continuity, current-sense scale, gate-off time, or external serial timing has been measured. The full GNU Arm CMake executable/runtime link and programming workflow have not been executed in this environment; object compilation is not a verified flash image. The linker/build files are provided for the installed course toolchain workflow and need its final build/program check.
Simulation uses ideal ADC values and a fixed clock, not a physical coil/field model. Static timing checks internal synchronous paths for the selected tool/device model; external interlock propagation and SPI setup/hold still require the scope tests in docs/bringup.md. Yosys reports its usual limited tri-state-support warning for MISO; the top-level pad is routed successfully and must be checked on the board.
The report is rendered and local navigation checked as part of delivery. Course-final evidence remains outstanding: actual parts and quotes, CAD schematics, measured results, team biographies, photographs, demo video, instructor checkoff, and publication. See docs/checkoff.md for the proposed test matrix.

DIGITAL LOGIC / 03

title: Control, clock by clock.
text:
The acquisition pipeline
The nominal 24 MHz internal timebase produces a 100 µs scan frame. The MCP3204 sequencer acquires CH0 current → CH1 primary Hall → CH2 reference Hall, then exposes a coherent snapshot and sample identifier.
ADC SPI runs at approximately 0.857 MHz. Three conversions and chip-select gaps occupy approximately 87 µs. Sampling begins 2.5 µs after every other PWM start, but the variable falling edge can still cross the acquisition window. Analog filtering and scope captures remain necessary.

title: Control, clock by clock.
text:
Fixed-point regulation
The PI controller works in raw ADC counts and PWM ticks. Gains use Q8.8 scaling: kp_q8 / 256 is ticks per count, while ki_q8 / 256 is ticks per count per 100 µs update.
Seven registered arithmetic stages complete in less than 0.3 µs at the nominal clock. Intermediate widths and gain bounds are explicit; the integrator is limited to ±1080 × 256. Removing enable clears PI history.

title: Control, clock by clock.
text:
Faults stay latched

Packet integrity and freshnessSerial CRC logic checks the command payload; malformed, short, corrupted, or repeated-sequence commands cannot refresh the watchdog. Command validation completes about 5 µs after chip select rises.
Four fault sourcesFault bits report external interlock loss, sampled overcurrent, command timeout, and ADC scan timeout. Faults remain latched until a valid clear sequence satisfies the health conditions.
Clear is separate from armClearing requires a disabled valid command, a recent scan, a healthy external input, and current below the requested hard limit. Arming is a subsequent action. Default uncommissioned builds keep output disabled.

PWM duty changes at a period boundary during normal operation. A fault or loss of permission can truncate a pulse. The proposed physical interlock is independent of telemetry refresh and must be validated on the actual board.

  THE IDEA
  A balancing act,every millisecond.Magnetic suspension is an unstable equilibrium. Pull too hard and the object rises into the coil. Pull too little and gravity takes over.This project explores that balance with Hall sensing and nested feedback. The STM32 estimates the gap and requests current. The UPduino regulates that current and supervises the output independently.Follow the control loop →

        ◎THREE ANALOG CHANNELSMeasure the field. Account for the current.Two linear Hall sensors and an inline current sensor feed a 12-bit MCP3204. The FPGA sequences all three channels into a coherent scan. Separating object motion from the coil’s own field is the first experimental challenge.Explore the sensing hardware →
        x̂1 kHz / POSITION CONTROLTranslate a field into a gap.The STM32 combines both Hall readings with measured current using a calibrated local model. Filtered velocity and a bounded position controller produce the next current request. Calibration coefficients and gains await physical measurements.Read the MCU design →
